introduction: Mírzá Yaḥyá, called Azal, was Bahá’u’lláh’s younger half-brother and the Báb’s nominal successor; he opposed Bahá’u’lláh’s claim, the community divided in Adrianople in the 1860s, and he died in Cyprus in 1912 with few followers. This guide gathers what Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wrote about him: grief at a brother “reared” and protected who turned in envy, an account of his conduct, appeals to inquirers to go and see for themselves, and instructions to meet his partisans’ slanders without retaliation. It is one side’s testimony, and is offered as such by its arc. Scripture knows the pattern of the brother or friend turned enemy in Cain, Joseph’s brothers, Absalom, Korah, Miriam and Aaron, and the Psalmist’s “mine own familiar friend”; Shakespeare knows it in Lear and Claudius, Aesop in the frozen serpent that reading 36 retells. Gamaliel’s “if this work be of men, it will come to nought” is the test the readings apply, the verse of mubáhalih is the Qur’anic practice reading 53 describes, and Proverbs and Mill state the duty of anyone reading a contested history: hear the other side.
questions: The readings speak more of grief than of anger. Find three passages where that is so. Why does betrayal by a brother wound differently from persecution by an enemy?
“He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.” What would a fair inquiry into this rupture require, and what do readings 61 and 63 themselves recommend?
Gamaliel’s test is the outcome: what is “of men” comes to nothing. Readings 70 and 75 apply it. What are the strengths and the weaknesses of judging a religious claim by its results?
Reading 74 asks for outward kindness to opponents and reading 78 for detachment from them; reading 80 asks that time be given to winning them. How do these fit together?
Reading 50 says the new community had become like the old one it left. What does that warning ask of any religious community, including the one giving it?
What does this guide teach about how to speak of those one believes have done great wrong?

outside.why: “O My brother, who hast slandered Me after I reared thee.” The Psalmist: it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: but it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance.
Seeing the rising fame of the Cause, he was filled with arrogance. Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
Joseph’s brothers, when they saw that their father loved him more: they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.
“Didst thou ever find Me willing to harm any created thing?” Abel to Cain in the Qur’an: even if thou stretch out thy hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against thee.
He attributed to the other all that he himself had committed. False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not. They rewarded me evil for good.
He withdrew and lived alone, that the fire of hatred might be stilled. Abram to Lot: let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee; for we be brethren. And they parted.
A brother who lived for years “under the wing of mercy”. Lear: how sharper than a serpent’s tooth it is to have a thankless child.
“Thou knowest that I protected my brother.” David, when the son who had risen against him was dead: O my son Absalom, my son, my son.
Hindered from remembrance by what a brother has done. Mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.
Better to have died a thousand times than that these matters become known. A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city.
From everyone on whom the most love was lavished came the worst. Blow, blow, thou winter wind. Thou art not so unkind as man’s ingratitude.
Imprisonments and exiles, and beyond them this. Paul’s list of dangers ends: in perils among false brethren.
What befell from one whose name had been exalted. A man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

The history of the rupture is told here by one of its parties and His son. Proverbs gives the rule of every court: he that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him. Readings 61 and 63 invite the reader to search. What can still be searched, and how should a reader hold an account that comes from one side?
Seeing covert rebellion, Bahá’u’lláh went alone to the mountains for two years. Then was Jesus led up of the spirit into the wilderness.
The one who claimed to be vicegerent hid in a thousand places. The hireling seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth.

“These affairs are like unto the foam upon the sea.” The image is the Qur’an’s: the flood beareth swelling foam; as for the foam, it passeth away as scum upon the banks, while that which is of use to mankind remaineth in the earth.
His envy became virulent and a rupture unavoidable. The Lord to Cain: why art thou wroth? If thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.
Officials found an instrument in the Báb’s nominee. Absalom at the gate, flattering every petitioner: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
He imagined his sedition would harm the Cause. Gamaliel’s counsel: if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: but if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.
When he saw another’s name renowned. Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.
He who could not speak in His presence rose to take His life. Claudius: my offence is rank; it hath the primal eldest curse upon’t, a brother’s murder.
The one strengthened and taught rose up like a serpent. The voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.

“We sheltered the speckled serpent in winter beneath My tent, yet when the sun of summer shone forth it stirred and bit Me.” The reading uses Aesop’s fable: a woodman put a frozen serpent in his bosom to warm, and by the fire it raised its head to sting his child.
He came from behind the veil and sought to cut down the Tree. Korah against Moses: ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy.
“We stood firm in days wherein the feet of every mighty soul did slip.” At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
Taught a letter of the Tablet, he grew proud. Miriam and Aaron: hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?
Why was Azal rejected? Deuteronomy’s test of a claimant: if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken.
Follow not those who wax proud before the verses. Ye shall know them by their fruits.
No one opposed him; he rejected himself. They went out from us, but they were not of us.

“The world of the Bayán hath been transformed into the world of the Shí‘ih”: the new community repeating the old one’s habits. Jesus of those in Moses’ seat: they say, and do not. Why do reform movements so often reproduce what they left?

The day of mubáhalih in Adrianople, when the challenger did not appear. The practice rests on this verse: come! we will summon our sons and your sons, and ourselves and yourselves, then we will pray humbly and invoke the curse of Allah upon those who lie.
The biblical scene of the same kind, on Carmel: how long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him.
He wrote in all directions, attributing his own acts to another. A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.
A sister whose coldness comes from love for Yaḥyá. He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.
Let seekers go to Cyprus and see his condition with their own eyes. Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.
Look at his books in his own handwriting in the London library. The Bereans searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

Mill’s rule for every inquirer: he who knows only his own side of the case, knows little of that. The reading sends its readers to the opponent’s own books. How many who study this history have done what readings 61 and 63 ask?
“The oppressor became oppressed” in a scholar’s account. Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light.

After the Báb’s martyrdom he taught no one and built nothing. Gamaliel’s precedent: Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.
Two of his partisans abroad: “outwardly treat them with kindness”. If thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink.
Forty years in freedom and not one soul guided. These three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none.
Be steadfast, and detach thyself. Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.

“Dedicate all your time to them, perhaps they will turn.” Ezekiel: when the wicked man turneth away from his wickedness, he shall save his soul alive. Reading 78 says to shun; reading 80 to give them all one’s time. What decides between the two?
Their slanders are beyond description. Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously.

The Cause suffered one blow through Yaḥyá and another later. Paul, of rivals who preached out of envy to add to his troubles: what then? every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice. Is anything like that largeness possible toward a rival claimant, on the readings’ account?
To be a Branch is conditional on turning to the Centre. I am the vine, ye are the branches: he that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
Many who followed the later rebel are coming back. This thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
But for the power of the Covenant, what would people have done? Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
“He whom I protected by My sovereignty denied Me.” He came unto his own, and his own received him not.

shortfall: Half the guide retells one event in closely similar words (the brother reared and protected, who rose in envy), and the readings of stretches seven and eight make specific charges about named persons that no outside text should seem to confirm; companions were placed on the themes, and those charges were left to stand as the readings’ own.

proverbs-brother-offended.text: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle

proverbs-who-is-able-to-stand-before-env.text: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy

quran-invoke-the-curse-of-allah.text: And whoso disputeth with thee concerning him, after the knowledge which hath come unto thee, say (unto him): Come! We will summon our sons and your sons, and our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves, then we will pray humbly (to our Lord) and (solemnly) invoke the curse of Allah upon those who lie.

shakespeare-a-brothers-murder.text: O, my offence is rank it smells to heaven; / It hath the primal eldest curse upon't, / A brother's murder

aesop-woodman-and-serpent.text: he saw it was a Serpent to all appearance dead. But he took it up and put it in his bosom to warm while he hurried home … the Serpent raised its head and put out its fangs and was about to sting the child to death
